A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Athena research. All 23 pages of v3 and 26 pages of v5, including equations, tables, figures and appendices, support comparison despite reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: V3 reports original Athena benchmark evaluations, process-label accuracy experiments, ablations, scaling analyses and reward-ranked fine-tuning results.

after.justification: V5 retains those original results and adds supplementary scaling, training-dynamics and thinking-completer findings.

M1.justification: Consistency filtering with weak and strong completers, ORM initialization, negative up-sampling, minimum-step reward aggregation and reward-ranked fine-tuning remain unchanged. The new pipeline diagram and inference pseudocode document the existing method.

E1.justification: The training sources, seven multimodal benchmarks, two text-only benchmarks, VisualProcessBench and PRM800K labeling test are retained. The thinking-model pilot changes the completer configuration without reporting a new dataset or task.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark tables and retained ablations use the same comparators. The expanded Monte Carlo scaling curve varies an existing comparator's training size; the thinking model is tested as a completer, not a new competing reward method.

E3.justification: V5 Figure 4 introduces a vanilla Monte Carlo training-size sweep from approximately 5K to 300K, replacing v3's single MC-300K reference line. Appendix A.9 additionally tests DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B as a strong completer. Existing benchmark splits, decoding settings and training recipes remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V5 extends the data-efficiency analysis with the Monte Carlo size sweep, adds training-loss comparisons in Figure 5 and Appendix A.7, and investigates thinking-completer behavior in Appendix A.9. Earlier component ablations, reward-choice tests and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging Best-of-N results over five runtimes. V5 adds no seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or other uncertainty-reporting practice; its new curves do not introduce uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–11 retain their numerical results. V5 adds Monte Carlo scaling and training-loss curves, reports that the thinking completer labels more than 98% of steps correct, and supplies timing results in Table 12, including 12 hours versus 12 minutes for training.

T1.justification: The ORM/PRM objectives, soft and hard Monte Carlo estimation equations, and reward-aggregation formulas retain their mathematical content. No new formal assumptions, theorem, proof or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about 5K-sample efficiency, consistency filtering, training strategies and Athena performance. The headline improvements of 10.2 points on WeMath, 7.1 on MathVista and 3.9 F1 on VisualProcessBench are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix A.9 newly qualifies applicability to thinking models: their reflection can repair erroneous intermediate steps, making completion-based labels overwhelmingly positive. V5 also interprets the new loss curves as evidence of faster convergence with Athena-5K.

D1.justification: V5 supplements the existing training recipe with inference pseudocode, explicit step and boxed-answer formatting, Math-Verify answer checking, and links to evaluation resources. Appendix A.8 and Table 12 disclose absolute annotation and training times. These additions do not establish changes to the existing implementation or experiments.

R1.justification: V5 adds Lee et al. (2025), Rethinking Reward Models for Multi-Domain Test-Time Scaling, to the PRM and thinking-model discussion. Existing research positioning is largely retained; other bibliography changes mainly update metadata.

P1.justification: Related Work moves from Appendix B to Section 2, appendices are reorganized and expanded, and the LLM drafting disclosure is removed. Local copyediting includes correcting PRM-minium to PRM-minimum. Most existing scientific prose remains closely matched.

P2.justification: The TMLR format substantially changes typography, text width, author presentation, table styling and figure placement throughout. V5 adds pipeline Figure 2, loss Figure 5, Algorithm 1 and Table 12, and redraws the scaling plot with expanded axes, revised legends and an efficiency annotation.

improvement.justification: The added Monte Carlo scaling comparison and concrete timing disclosures make the existing efficiency claim easier to assess. The pipeline and inference explanations improve clarity, while Appendix A.9 identifies a useful applicability boundary. These are limited gains over unchanged central evidence; the thinking-model pilot remains sparsely specified and the inference example remains schematic.
